title: Light-induced rectified orbital magnetization in electron-hole bilayers
authors: Erlend Syljuåsen, Gabriel Cardoso, Esra Ilke Albar, Patrick J. Wong, Angel Rubio, Alexander V. Balatsky
abstract: Circularly polarized light can rectify orbital motion into a static magnetization through the inverse Faraday effect (IFE), but in electron-hole bilayers the electron and hole contributions cancel exactly when their properties are equivalent. We show that electron-hole bilayers in transition-metal dichalcogenide platforms avoid this cancellation through effective-mass asymmetry alone, and that the surviving orbital IFE is sensitive to interlayer coupling. In the weak-coupling regime, a two-component Drude description yields an induced magnetization of order one Bohr magneton per carrier for representative terahertz driving. In the strong-coupling regime, where the carriers bind into interlayer excitons, we treat the relative motion using a hydrogenic model with a Rytova-Keldysh interaction and obtain a reduced but finite response. We give closed-form expressions that allow estimates across a broad parameter range and identify where the response is largest.
summary: This work analyzes how circularly polarized light generates a rectified orbital magnetization in electron-hole bilayers, a phenomenon requiring inherent asymmetry between the electron and hole layers. The authors develop a comprehensive theoretical framework covering both weak-coupling (Drude) and strong-coupling (excitonic) regimes. The findings confirm that asymmetry is key to observing this magnetization, providing insights into tunable spintronic materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the light-induced rectified orbital magnetization in electron-hole bilayers, specifically addressing how structural asymmetry prevents the exact cancellation of electron and hole contributions.
main_result: The induced magnetization is non-zero due to electron-hole asymmetry, yielding a finite response in both the weak-coupling Drude limit and the strong-coupling excitonic regime.
method: The authors employ a combination of semiclassical Drude modeling for weak coupling and a quantum mechanical hydrogenic model for strong coupling, analyzing the response using time-dependent perturbation theory.
model_or_system: The system is an electron-hole bilayer, modeled using transition-metal dichalcogenide platforms. The Hamiltonian is treated in two limits: a two-component Drude model for weak coupling, and a hydrogenic model with a Rytova-Keldysh interaction for interlayer excitons.

important_parameters: Effective mass asymmetry ($m_e/m_h$), interlayer coupling strength ($\gamma$), and the driving frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The Drude model is limited to weakly correlated carriers, and the strong-coupling analysis assumes an effective hydrogenic potential.

paper_structure: The paper progresses from the general problem statement, develops the weak-coupling Drude description, analyzes the crossover via drag resistivity, and finally tackles the strong-coupling regime using a quantum excitonic model.
why_interesting: The interplay between light-matter interaction, orbital magnetism, and the crossover between semiclassical (Drude) and strongly correlated (excitonic) regimes is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics.

The wave functions are of the form ψn,m(r, φ) = Rn,m(r)eimφ, where (r, φ) are polar coordinates of the relative coordinate. States with ±m are degenerate because the field-free relative-motion Hamiltonian only depends on |m|.
